_comment: ci-reorg-target-debt gate policy (DATA, not code). North-Star Completion Programme bootstrap step T3b: Global Binding Rule 1 (no-new-reorg-target-debt), normative from this gate's admission onward. The six reorg-target forms live HERE as data — the Rust kernel hardcodes no oyatie-specific prefix, path, or name, so another repo adopts this gate by editing this policy (pipeline-as-product). Existing target-prefix estate is migration inventory covered shrink-only by the committed baseline; anything NEW under a target form fails closed. Rule authority: Global Binding Rule 1 became NORMATIVE at bootstrap T2 via the founder execution-authorization record evidence/goals/north-star-completion-t2-execution-authorization-20260812.json (its global_binding_rule_1 block names the rule, the six target forms, the normative-from point, and the overturn/exemption path); the approved plan is content-pinned by sha256 95132e4e2ef165667223117a026e3c3d5856a45250b4a7101b7cefef5ddd6ab1 in the T1 receipt, with full-text repository archival deferred to the Wave 1 retired-vocabulary carve-out. Bootstrap evidence: evidence/goals/north-star-completion-t1-hold-lift-receipt-20260812.json, evidence/goals/north-star-completion-t2-execution-authorization-20260812.json, evidence/goals/north-star-completion-option-b-contingency-contract-20260812.json.

target_forms._comment: The six reorg-target forms of Global Binding Rule 1. name_prefixes bind NEW crate/module/binary names and workspace dependency names (Arm B and the dep-name half of audit mode); path_prefixes bind NEW tracked files (Arm A) and NEW work-item evidence anchors (Arm C).

adoption._comment: Repository-instance identity consumed as DATA by the neutral engine and generated SCM face. `initial_adoption_base_sha` is the exact protected-base merge commit immediately before this gate first lands; it must be refreshed if the bootstrap PR is rebased before admission. Once live, the immutable merge-base policy freezes both values.

baseline._comment: Arm A baseline strategy: a committed SORTED, DEDUPLICATED LIST OF PER-PATH DIGESTS — the lowercase sha256 hex of each tracked target-prefix path string at gate-authoring time — plus the Arm B dep-digest inventory (path-dep entries are digests of the (declaring-manifest, dependency-name, normalized-destination) tuple so a new edge to an already-baselined destination is still NEW debt) and the Arm C anchor inventory (anchors stay literal; verified free of scanner-relevant tokens). Digests, not literal paths: the committed file must carry none of the retired vocabulary embedded in migration-inventory path names (brand-residue ratchet blocks NEW files carrying those tokens), while exact set semantics are preserved. Born-blocking zero-NEW ratchet: the gate hashes each LIVE target-prefix path and a digest absent from the list fails closed reporting the exact violating LIVE path. SHRINK-ONLY: removals are always admissible, and a removal REQUIRES baseline regeneration in the same change — a baseline digest matching no live path fails the gate (stale-row detection, mirroring the gate-coverage-baseline re-freeze convention) as a count plus digest-prefix bucket with the regeneration command in the failure message, so burned-down debt can never silently regain headroom. Widening the Arm B path-dep key from destination-only to the edge-identity tuple is a reviewed initial freeze (same rationale as the prior name-surface widening): regenerate via the policy-declared --regen-baseline surface after temporarily moving the committed baseline aside so the missing-file adoption path can snapshot the live estate.
baseline.regeneration_enforces_shrink_only: The --regen-baseline surface itself refuses expansion: the candidate snapshot is compared with the committed baseline and ANY added path/dep/name/anchor is a hard RTD_BASELINE_EXPANSION refusal, so the documented regeneration workflow cannot launder new debt into the baseline. A missing baseline file is the initial-adoption freeze; expanding coverage is a reviewed governance act on the committed file, never a regeneration side effect.

exemptions._comment: Empty at birth. Each future entry is a reviewed path or path-prefix excluded from Arms A/C and audit mode, carrying its own justification; expansion is a governance act, never a gate-side default.

scan._comment: Read-only filesystem walk parameters for the live-tree collector. On a clean checkout the walk over the target-prefix roots with these directory names skipped equals the git-tracked set exactly (verified at gate authoring); untracked residue under a target prefix fails closed by design.

workspace_manifest._comment: Arm B input, half one: the root workspace manifest's dependency table (inline-table and subsection forms; double- OR single-quoted path values; relative spellings are lexically normalized before evaluation; a path value the parser cannot read is a fail-closed RTD_DEP_PATH_UNPARSEABLE finding). Cargo members are NOT required to inherit through this table, so Arm B additionally scans every member manifest and declared name via name_surface below.

name_surface._comment: Arm B input, half two: the repo-wide name-and-member-dependency surface the target NAME prefixes bind. Every Cargo manifest contributes its [package] name, [[bin]] names, and path entries in the listed dependency sections — including target-qualified tables ([target.<triple-or-cfg>.dependencies], plus the dev-/build- variants and their [<section>.<name>] subsections) — resolved repo-relative against the declaring manifest's directory; every Buck file contributes its literal target names. Existing target-form names and member path deps are migration inventory carried shrink-only by the committed baseline, keyed by the (declaring-manifest, dependency-name, normalized-destination) tuple so a new edge to an already-baselined destination is still NEW debt; minting a NEW target-form crate/binary/build-target name or a NEW member path dependency into a target prefix fails closed.

masterplan._comment: Arm C input: the parsed planning SSOT. Target-path anchors are lexically normalized and keyed by the nearest owning object's first stable identity field in the declared precedence plus the anchor field/name. Array indices are never identity, so unrelated insertions and reordering cannot flap the ratchet. A target anchor without a stable owner fails closed. The two pre-existing owned-stack anchors are carried shrink-only under their stable rung identities.

reduction_claims._comment: Arm D contract: an artifact object asserting a net target-surface-reduction claim is refused unless it binds the measurement: all companion fields present, the two count fields NUMERIC, and after_count strictly below before_count — a claim whose own numbers demonstrate growth (or nonnumeric counts) is refused. The gate still mints no numeric threshold: the only comparison is the direction the claim itself asserts; any future corridor slot stays a NAMED PLACEHOLDER routed to the Wave 5 corridor freeze (see corridor_placeholders). Beyond the planning SSOT, every *.json artifact under scan_roots is evaluated for claims (an absent root contributes nothing; an unparseable artifact under a scan root fails closed).

audit_mode._comment: Deterministic interval audit over an explicit commit range <from>..<to>. Audit-capture Git I/O stays at the CALLER boundary: the caller materializes a captured commit-set JSON and the binary's audit engine — the SAME code path the fixture suite proves — evaluates it. The live admission path consumes a separately materialized immutable origin/dev merge-base policy+baseline snapshot. FAIL-CLOSED: a missing, unparseable, empty, incomplete (complete != true, or a commit missing any fact array), range-less, range-unbound (captured commits must exactly equal authoritative_commits from the SCM boundary, in order, and the last must be range.to), or malformed input is a non-zero explicit RTD_AUDIT_INPUT_INVALID finding, never a pass. Captured dep paths are normalized repo-relative against the declaring-manifest origin before the prefix test, matching live Arm B. A commit introducing a file/dep/name/anchor under a target form relative to the range base is reported per commit and per arm. Bootstrap audit accepts only a clean zero-finding interval: candidate-authored remediation prose is rejected until a separately protected disposition mechanism exists. The report is machine-readable JSON suitable for committing as a durable evidence record.
commit_set_materialization: The caller (coordinator) materializes the captured input for <from>..<to> with plain git, outside this crate:
1a. authoritative_commits: the SCM boundary emits the exact same ordered rev-list and the audit requires byte-for-byte array equality with commits[*].sha; complete=true is not authority by itself

2. per commit added_paths: git diff-tree -m --no-commit-id --name-only --diff-filter=A -r <sha> (the producer treats output as a set so merge-commit parent duplicates collapse; -m is mandatory so conflict-resolution additions created by a merge commit are not omitted)

3. per commit added_workspace_path_deps / added_dep_names: dependency entries and declared names present on the Arm B surface (root workspace table, member-manifest dependency sections including target-qualified tables, package/bin/Buck target names, and Rust module declarations) at <sha> and absent at <sha>^ (objects {name, path, origin}; origin is the declaring manifest and is required whenever path is non-empty so the audit can normalize relative spellings; name-only entries carry an empty string path)
4. per commit added_evidence_anchors: anchor strings (per masterplan.anchor_field_names) present in the planning SSOT at <sha> and absent at <sha>^
5. set range.from/range.to to the exact shas and complete=true only when every authoritative commit in the range carries all four fact arrays; remediation_records must be [] in bootstrap mode

liveness._comment: Every run — blocking and audit — emits evaluated_path_count and the evaluated_arms list in its report. A missing scheduled run is a GAP, never a pass: absence of a report is absence of evidence, and no consumer may treat a silent interval as green.

corridor_placeholders._comment: No numeric threshold is minted by this gate. Any future numeric corridor slot (e.g. a maximum admissible target-surface size) is a named placeholder resolved only by the Wave 5 corridor freeze.

product_contract.born_pack_shaped: Target forms, baseline location, scan parameters, manifest/masterplan paths, anchor field names, claim schema, and exemptions are DATA here; the Rust kernel fixes only the evaluation ALGORITHM.
product_contract.ratchet: Born-blocking at the committed baseline and immutable origin/dev merge-base ceiling: the live tree is green at ZERO new debt, so a candidate cannot waive a NEW target-form file, dependency edge, declaration name, or anchor by adding its hash to the same-change baseline.
product_contract.execution: Buck2-native Rust gate under //ci/facade/reorg-target-debt; enforced by the required buck2 lane (buck2 test //ci/...) behind oya-ci-required.

purpose: No-new-reorg-target-debt gate (Global Binding Rule 1). Arm A refuses new tracked files under reorg-target path prefixes against a shrink-only committed baseline; Arm B refuses new dependency edges into target paths and new target-form Cargo package/dependency, Buck target, or Rust module declarations, all keyed by declaration identity; Arm C refuses work items whose evidence anchors point under target prefixes; Arm D resolves each net-debt-reduction census ref to a schema-valid repository snapshot whose claim and before/after counts match; audit mode replays Arms A-C over an explicit commit range and fails closed on incomplete input, merge-commit omissions, or unremediated findings.
